study_type_evidence.quote: The IRDye800-labeled target peptide (200 μM, 200 μL) was injected intravenously in Cpc;Apc mice
Peptide stability was evaluated by incubating 6 μL of 1 mM peptide in PBS at 37 °C
Cultures were grown in 6-well tissue culture plates (USA Scientific CytoOne, Ocala, FL, USA; #CC7682-7506) using Matrigel with growth media

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: NSG (NOD.Cg-PrkdcscidIl2rgtm1Wjl/SzJ), 7-12 weeks old, sex not reported; DSS-pretreated and implanted orthotopically with patient-derived colonoids
in_vivo_species.quote: 7–12-week-old NSG (NOD.Cg-PrkdcscidIl2rgtm1Wjl/SzJ, Jackson laboratory, #005557) mice were treated with 2.5% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) for 5 days

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: CPC;Apc genetically engineered mice with spontaneous distal colonic adenomas; sex, age and weight not reported. Used for the pharmacokinetic imaging, serum stability and safety studies
in_vivo_species.quote: CPC;Apc mice have been genetically engineered to sporadically delete an APC gene regulated by a Cre promoter

ex_vivo_detail: Serum stability assay: QQT*-IRDye800 was incubated at a final concentration of 30 μM in 194 μL of serum obtained from a CPC;Apc mouse at 37 °C, precipitated with acetonitrile and analysed by RP-HPLC at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 24 h, with relative concentration taken as peak area. The paper heads this section 'In Vivo Serum Stability', but the Methods describe incubation in harvested mouse serum, i.e. an ex vivo assay. Excised mouse colon and resected organs from dosed animals were also stained/imaged, but those are readouts of in vivo biodistribution rather than ex vivo treatments.
in_vitro_detail: Patient-derived human colonoids (a cMethigh adenoma, a cMetlow adenoma and a normal colonoid) cultured in Matrigel with LWRN conditioned medium; FFPE colonoid sections co-stained with 5 μM QQT*-IRDye800 or TLQ*-IRDye800 plus anti-cMet-AF488 antibody and imaged by confocal microscopy; cMet expression confirmed by immunohistochemistry.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: T/B ratios were measured between 0–48 h from CPC;Apc mice following intravenous injection of QQT*-IRDye800 (200 μM, 200 μL).
concentration_time_figure.note: Figure 5a plots target-to-background fluorescence ratio versus time from 0 to 48 h in living mice (imaging signal, not a measured plasma concentration). Figure 5b plots relative peptide remaining versus time in mouse serum, i.e. a percent-remaining-style ex vivo stability curve. Neither panel is a plasma concentration-time curve.

bioanalytical_method: Analytical RP-HPLC with peak-area quantification for serum stability; NIR fluorescence imaging for all in vivo and organ measurements, using a modified rigid small-animal endoscope (lambda-ex 785 nm) and a Pearl Trilogy imager (lambda-ex 785 nm, lambda-em 820 nm)
bioanalytical_quote: The relative peptide concentrations were determined by measuring the area under the peak (Waters, Breeze 2).
notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE HALF-LIFE. The only half-life in the body, 3.6 h, comes from incubating the peptide in serum harvested from a CPC;Apc mouse at 37 °C and following it by RP-HPLC over 24 h. It is a proteolytic stability half-life measured ex vivo, not a plasma elimination half-life from a dosed animal, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both half_life_absorption and half_life_elimination are 'not reported'. The paper's own section heading 'In Vivo Serum Stability' is misleading relative to its Methods; the matrix field records the assay as it was actually performed. No plasma or blood concentrations were ever measured in this study, so there is no Cmax, tmax or AUC. The in vivo pharmacokinetics section is entirely imaging-based: 'Quantified intensities showed a peak T/B ratio at 1 h after injection of QQT*-IRDye800. The signal decreased to the baseline by ~24 h post-injection', and Figure 5a gives 'a mean (±SD) value of 2.2 ± 0.4 at 1 h post-injection with clearance by ~24 h'. That 1 h peak is a tumour-to-background fluorescence ratio maximum, not a plasma tmax, so it was deliberately not entered in the tmax field. Dose is reported only as a concentration and volume (200 μM, 200 μL); no body weight normalised dose is given. Human involvement was limited to donor-derived colonoid tissue (adenoma from a 46-year-old male and a 64-year-old male, normal colon from a 43-year-old female deceased donor) cultured in vitro; no human subject was dosed, so clinical_detail is null. Biodistribution at 1 h showed strong kidney signal consistent with renal clearance, with increased liver and lung intensity attributed to vasculature; no toxicity was seen on necropsy, hematology or chemistry at 48 h.
